main_text.head: CAPVT TERTIVM.
main_text.p: Lectio 18.4. Decembr.1581[?]FIlum & feriem orationis Prophetæ Habacuc in hoc capite ultimo, pridé Usu.tradidimus in Prolegomenis. Istud autē satis fuerit initiò monere, Prophetā nostrum suo exemplo nos docere, non esse nobis intuentibus tristia Ecclesiæ & singulorum piorum fata, nimium indulgendum dolori, nec immorandum disquisitioni curiosæ iudiciorum Dei, quæ longè uincunt captum nostrum: sed potius nostram ignorantiam & infirmitatem agnoscendam, & præclara bonitatis, iustitiæ & uirtutis diuinæ specimina repetenda: ut eorum meditatio confirmandæ in nobis fidei & spei seruiat. Vtrumque enim nobis considerandū est, & quid nos deceat, & quid nos non deceat. Decet nos opera & beneficia Dei memoria repetere, ut celebretur eorum auctor Deus, qui est mirabilis in cunctis suis operibus. Non decet τὰ ἀσυγγνώμονα[?] & abstrusa, quæ Deus in sua solius potestate posuit, curiosè scrutari. Prudenter Gregorius: Rationem, inquit, de occulto Dei iudi-

page.notes: The left-margin notes "Lectio 18." and "4. Decembr." are clear. The third margin line, "1581", is very small and faint and is uncertain. The note "Vsu." is printed as "Vsu." and was changed to "Usu." under the u/v rule. The Greek word after "non decet" is hard to read at this size; the reading ἀσυγγνώμονα is a best guess. The catchword "cio" is the start of the next word, "iudicio". The first word is printed with a large initial F, joined to the word as "FIlum". The page number "190" is printed in a worn form.
